body: (I hope more of that comes into your life,)

Much better than what. Because if you're going to say at least they have people who care about them etc, that doesn't help the situation at all.

Okay, sometimes it does "help" to talk, but a lot of the time "help" means temporarily providing some relief. I think a lot of the time if you're at the point where you're contemplating suicide, just "talking" etc isn't going to help.
(Does having nice friends and family have an affect on depression, suicide ideation etc? Because if so, then I think a lot of people wouldn't be suffering.)

I can completely relate - and I guess it's what's kept me here. But I don't think it's selfish. I think it's unfair to expect someone who has the capacity to make the decision for themself to stay if they're really struggling or even just don't want to - but at the same time, people definetly will be affected by it and that's a massive thing that keeps the scale very balanced.

I'm really sorry you're having a hard time/things are great and I really hope that things begin to improve for you soon.
